instruction: Create a formula in cell B1 that calculates the total sum of marks in one of the marks columns using the SUM function

metadata.explanation: Task requires creating a SUM formula in B1 that sums marks from one column. Evaluator analyzes the actual Excel file to identify marks columns (columns with numeric data), then validates that the formula references a valid marks column and covers at least 70% of data rows or uses an entire column reference (e.g., D:D).

llm_judge_reasons: Complete semantic coverage: Evaluator verifies all instruction requirements - SUM function presence, formula in cell B1, references marks column
Dynamic file analysis: Metric loads actual Excel file and identifies marks columns programmatically by detecting numeric data columns, avoiding hardcoded assumptions
Correct data validation: Validates formula references actual marks columns identified from file structure (not hardcoded column letters)
Proper coverage checking: Validates formula covers at least 70% of data rows OR uses entire column reference (D:D), ensuring comprehensive sum
Instruction-evaluator alignment: Instruction specifies 'marks in one of the marks columns' and evaluator correctly validates single-column sum with proper coverage
Robust fallback logic: If file analysis fails, falls back to structural validation ensuring evaluator doesn't fail completely
Correct parameter handling: Metric correctly accesses expected.get('contains') when expected.type='rule', as expected receives the rules dict directly from get_rule()
State freshness: Postconfig includes Ctrl+S to save file before evaluation, ensuring fresh state for getter to read
Proper formula extraction: Getter uses openpyxl with data_only=False to correctly extract formulas (not computed values)
